subject: Proposed post-dated invoice schedule & provisional credit safety net
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediq.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request: post-dated invoice cadence + Net60 / provisional credit

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. Finance asked me to propose a billing cadence that matches our internal treasury windows: we'd like to request Net60 terms for the pilot, paid via a staggered post-dated invoice schedule (two invoices per month, dated for the 15th and 30th) for the first two quarters.

To make this work internally, Mediq is also asking for a provisional credit buffer of $150,000 while we get the pilot underway. We understand you may need additional controls — happy to agree to monitoring and milestone triggers.

One more thing: our EU subsidiary handles the service, so we'd prefer the invoices to be issued to Mediq EU BV (NL) and for VAT to be handled via reverse charge. I'll attach the preliminary PO and our VAT certificate for review.

Attachments: prelim_PO_8765.pdf

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept post-dated invoices and the proposed credit buffer? If helpful, we can set a quick call with procurement this week.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Head of Procurement — Mediq Health Systems
oliver.grant@mediq.com
+44 20 7222 1000

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediq.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: post-dated invoice cadence + Net60 / provisional credit

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear proposal and for sending the PO. Appreciate the detail on the EU entity. Quick points from our side: 

- We can support staged/post-dated invoice scheduling operationally, but that flows into our credit policy. For a Net60 request with a provisional $150k buffer we typically require one of the following: a) a refundable security deposit equal to 25% of the buffer, b) an early-payment incentive on the first two invoices, or c) an elevated credit check + weekly reporting plus a defined ramp schedule.

- Alternative offer: Net45 with a $100k provisional credit cap and an agreed 30% prepayment on the first invoice. This often hits the right balance between your treasury needs and our AR risk profile.

- To enable reverse-charge VAT on invoices, we'll need the Mediq EU BV VAT registration number and the VAT certificate (EU) as part of onboarding. Please confirm the exact billing entity name and VAT number.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm billing entity + upload VAT cert;
- We run a quick credit check and propose a provisional cap (turnaround ~48 hours);
- If accepted, we produce a credit addendum (DocuSign) and a post-dated invoice schedule you can sign.

I'm looping Marissa (AR) to draft the addendum and Rishi (tax/compliance) for VAT handling. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to iron out details.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Office: +1 415 555 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediq.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: post-dated invoice cadence + Net60 / provisional credit

Oliver / Naomi — thanks for the context. From AR perspective here's a pragmatic approach we can offer if Mediq signs the addendum:

- Initial provisional credit threshold: $100,000 for first 60 days. If payments arrive on time for 60 consecutive days, threshold increases to $200,000.
- Post-dated invoice acceptance: we will accept invoices dated on agreed schedule; payment due dates will still count from the invoice date. No penalty-free re-dating beyond the signed schedule.
- If total outstanding > provisional threshold for more than 10 business days, we will request a security deposit (25% of excess) or convert remaining invoices to Net30 until balance drops.
- If remit lag consistently exceeds 60 days, AR reserves the right to pause provisioning until remediation or to require an irrevocable standby letter of credit.

I've attached our credit-addendum-template.docx for your review and a DocuSign link to speed up execution once terms are agreed. If Mediq prefers Net60 as an immutable term, we'd need an up-front 25% deposit.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/XYZ-abc-sign

Marissa Cole
Director, Accounts Receivable — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0188

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@mediq.com>, accounts@mediq.com
Date: 2026-08-20T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: post-dated invoice cadence + Net60 / provisional credit

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. Mediq can do an initial $125k provisional cap with a commitment to move to $200k after 45 days of on-time payments. We can't provide a 25% deposit for the pilot, but we can agree to the security deposit if we cross the provisional threshold.

Per Naomi's ask, attached is our VAT certificate for Mediq EU BV and the VAT number is NL123456789B01. Please confirm you can invoice Mediq EU BV and include reverse-charge language; our AP team will route payments through the NL entity.

Attachments: mediq_vat_certificate.pdf

Please confirm bank details and the invoice remit instructions so we can map the post-dated schedule into our ERP. If you can get the credit addendum to us as a DocuSign today, we'll push it through procurement.

Best,
Oliver

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: VAT evidence + final settlement plan recommendation

Internal notes / action items before we sign: 

- VAT: mediq_vat_certificate.pdf looks valid; we still need a company extract showing Mediq EU BV is the registered legal entity. Request that from Oliver (or have procurement upload). Reverse charge is fine for NL -> Redwoods invoices if entity is correct and VAT number validates.

- Settlement recommendation: accept the agreed compromise: Net45 with a provisional credit cap at $150,000. Structure the first two post-dated invoices as follows: 30% due on invoice 1 (30 days), 40% due on invoice 2 (45 days), remaining 30% due on invoice 3 (75 days) — this gives Mediq treasury some runway while shortening our exposure.

- Execution requirements: signed credit-addendum (DocuSign), VAT cert (received), company extract, and the signed SOW attached to the DocuSign package. AR to enable the post-dated schedule only after those items are in place.

I'll ask legal to add a short tax/responsibility clause in the SOW and have Marissa queue the addendum. Naomi, please confirm and I will mark the deal ready for finance sign-off.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance & Tax Compliance — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 650 555 0172
